text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: DETECTED: CloudKV (managed-cache.cloudkv.net) - elevated 5xx + latency on cache GETs. Rate limiter adapters are falling back to DB. Paging @olivia (oncall).

olivia: Oncall — ack. Thanks for the ping. Mike, can you share scope (hosts / regions / customer impact)?

mike: digging in. Seeing spike from the CloudKV SDK: connection resets and 502/504s across eu-west-1 and us-east-1. Affected paths: /generate (tokenization cache) and /embeddings/read cache. Sample error from node logs:

```
ERR cache_adapter:cloudkv get failed key=prefix:session:xyz err="502 Bad Gateway"
stack: ConnectionResetError at poll()
```

mike: Also noticing our rate limiter's cache misses increased ~18x, which pushed more calls to downstream DB and caused backend latency to spike. 95th p99 latency for /v1/generate went from ~220ms -> ~2.1s in spikes.

tara: Is this a total outage for CloudKV or partial degradations? Any vendor bulletin?

mike: No vendor public bulletin yet. Vendor API status shows some warnings in eu-west. Telemetry indicates intermittent TLS handshake failures and occasional >500 responses.

kevin: Support is getting customer reports: several small customers seeing timeouts and a handful of higher-volume customers hitting request throttles. I have a list: AcmeCorp (hosted), BrightApp (hosted), and two internal QA stacks. Most dedicated customers on Reserved capacity not impacted.

eva: For status page: suggested message draft:

"We are investigating elevated error rates with our managed cache provider affecting response times and some requests returning errors. Engineers are actively mitigating and we're routing traffic to fallback caches. We will provide updates every 30 minutes."

olivia: Agreed. Locking down mitigation steps. Mike/Tara — propose immediate mitigations:
- Enable local in-memory LRU fallback for cache misses on API tier.
- Reduce write-through refreshes (disable background warmers) to avoid thundering herd.
- Temporarily increase per-customer rate-limiter token bucket to allow graceful degradation, and enable request queuing on gateway for bursts.
- Start draining non-critical batch jobs that cause cache churn.

tara: I can push the feature flag for local fallback. Config change (K8s configmap) we'll apply to api-deployment in eu-west first:

```
FEATURE_FLAGS:
  ENABLE_LOCAL_CACHE_FALLBACK: "true"
  CACHE_REFRESH_DISABLED: "true"
```

mike: I'll implement the rate-limiter adjustment. Command to flip bucket for hosted customers (rolling change):

```
./rlctl set-global --burst 1.5x --window 60s
```

mike: Applying to eu-west now, then us-east after verifying.

(5m later)

mike: Rolled local fallback to 25% of nodes in eu-west as canary. Immediate reduction in 5xx seen on canary nodes. Error rate on canary from 11.8% -> 1.9% within 90s.

kevin: Updating customers now with ETA. Sending BrightApp note: "We are seeing degraded cache provider behaviour causing elevated latencies. We've activated a fallback cache and expect improved responses within ~5-10 minutes."

eva: Posting status: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/1810009999 (draft posted)

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Action taken: local fallback enabled (canary), rate limiter burst increased, background refresh disabled. Monitoring.

mike: Metrics after canary: cache adapter error rate eu-west 5xx down from 12% -> 1.6%. DB QPS dropped by ~22% from peak. 95th latencies for affected endpoints down ~600-800ms. Proceeding with global rollout.

tara: Rolling to global now. Deploy plan: eu-west -> us-east -> ap-south. Each region 5min observation window. I will abort if error rate rises above 3%.

(25m later)

mike: Global rollout complete. Final numbers: error rate at 1.4% global, p95 latency back to ~240ms. We're still seeing occasional blips in CloudKV (vendor-side) but platform impact largely mitigated.

olivia: Good work. Next steps:
- Open an incident with CloudKV support and request RCA and timeline for full resolution.
- Schedule follow-up postmortem and update runbook to include local-fallback as an automated mitigation.
- Prepare a customer postmortem for major affected accounts (AcmeCorp, BrightApp).

kevin: I'll draft customer postmortem and coordinate with account owners.

mike: I've filed a ticket with CloudKV (Ref: CKV-987654) and requested escalation; attaching logs and timing. Also asking for SLA credit details.

eva: Scheduling follow-up update in 2 hours, and will include links to metrics and timeline. Good to close active page when vendor confirms stability.

olivia: Handoff: I'm wrapping up the active mitigation. Handoff to @jorge who is oncall starting at 06:30Z.

olivia: Jorge, summary for handoff (copying into rotation):
- Issue: CloudKV intermittent 5xx/TLS failures causing increased cache misses and DB load.
- Mitigation applied: local in-memory fallback enabled, cache refresh disabled, rate-limiter burst increased, non-critical batches drained.
- Current state: error rate ~1.4%, p95 latency recovered. Vendor showing intermittent warnings.
- Actions for next oncall: monitor vendor status, follow-up with CloudKV for RCA, coordinate customer PMs.

jorge: Thanks — ack and will monitor. If vendor doesn't provide acceptable RCA by EOD, we should prepare contingency (multi-provider fallback).

olivia: Closing active paging. Incident classified as "dependency partial degradation". We'll keep incident open for vendor RCA and postmortem.

(reacted :thumbsup: by mike, tara, kevin)
